Parkinson’s disease pathway: Increases in calcium signaling and decreases in mitochondrial electron transport chain complexes in dopaminergic neurons

Parkinson’s disease pathway: Increases in calcium signaling and decreases in mitochondrial electron transport chain complexes in dopaminergic neurons. Upregulation of CAMKII signaling and decrease in PERK (A). Decrease in mitochondrial complexes I and III and Divalent Metal Transporter 1 (DMT1) ZRT/IRT-like proteins (ZIP) expression (B). Overall decrease in pathway activity for enzymes affected in Parkinson’s disease (C). Green indicates decrease, and red indicates an increase in PD pathway gene expression score. Gray genes participate in the PD pathway; white box genes do not participate in the pathway. Red text (PINK1) indicates a common mutation in the PD pathway
